title: Phone Habits May Reveal Stress Levels, Study Says
paragraphs: Most people use their smartphones many times a day. Now, a new study from South Korea suggests that the way people use their phones could reveal how stressed they are.

The study was carried out by researchers at KAIST, the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology, led by Professor Uichin Lee. It was presented in October 2026 at UbiComp/ISWC, an international technology conference in Shanghai, China.

The researchers developed an AI system that looks at people's everyday phone habits. Instead of only measuring how long people use certain apps, the system focuses on what people are actually doing, such as chatting, browsing the internet, making payments or writing emails.

The study involved 26 university students and office workers in their 20s and 30s, who all used Android phones. The researchers collected data from their phones for between one month and more than three months. Each day, the participants also reported whether they felt stressed.

The AI system identified 29 types of repeated phone behavior. Using this information, it was able to correctly predict whether participants had a stressful day about 75% of the time. This was better than a method that only looked at app usage. Interestingly, even looking only at messaging and payments worked better than the old method.
The researchers also tried to protect privacy. The system did not save the messages that people typed. It only recorded whether people typed text and how often.

However, the study had limitations. It was very small, and all the participants were young Android users. It also only found links between phone habits and stress. It did not show that certain behaviors cause stress. In addition, predictions that are correct about 75% of the time are far from perfect.
The researchers now plan to test the system with people of different ages and jobs.
